title: Review: adversarial Opus 5.5 confirmation pass (seventh)
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

SEVENTH PASS (adversarial Opus 5.5 confirmation). Prior: Sol .8.1/.8.4/.8.6/.8.8/.8.11 and Opus .8.14 (read .8.14 fully). Since .8.14: batch G (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.15) reversed design decision D2 (a dead combatant stays dead in BOTH death-rule modes, SRD rule:healing), and repaired S34 (combatant), S35, S36, S37, S38, S39, S40. (1) State CLOSED/OPEN for S34-S40 with fresh registry evidence. (2) Adversarially attack the batch G changes and their siblings (dead-terminal everywhere: update_combatant, admission/projection, actor upsert, effect cleanup, recovery, exhaustion; dying-turn availability vs begin_turn settlement; knockout boundaries). (3) A final fresh sweep of the whole PR for anything still unfound (IDs from S41). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly. Close with APPROVE-READY or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: Closure states plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
SEVENTH PASS (adversarial Opus 5.5 confirmation), bound to HEAD d4177b92, origin/main ae840498; rules-clause-complete. Probes are throwaway /tmp/rv16 scripts driving createDefaultToolRegistry().invoke; parity probes import the parent checkout (origin/main) read-only.

S41 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1838-1846 (start_encounter projection status: hpCurrent === 0 under monster rules => 'unconscious' only when actor.status is exactly 'unconscious', otherwise 'dead'), then syncCombatantActor writes the death to the canonical actor
Requirement/authority: batch-G supervisor decision for S38 (eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.15: projecting a monster-rules actor at 0 HP that was knocked out keeps it unconscious and leaves the canonical actor unchanged; 'only real terminal causes make it dead'); batch-E D1 (admission/projection must not invent a death); .19.5.7.5 'default behavior unchanged'; SRD rule:knocking-a-creature-out ('falls unconscious and is stable'); ADR 0020 state integrity. Consequence is now permanent because batch G made dead terminal (D2 reversed, SRD rule:healing).
Failure through registry (fresh, both branches): goblin actor 7/7 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-10,status:'unconscious') => 0/unconscious -> update_combatant(status:'inactive' | 'escaped') => 0/inactive|escaped (accepted; actor synced) -> close_combat_instance(completed) -> start_encounter(c2, actors:[{actorId:'gob'}]) => projection c2-gob 0/dead AND campaign actor rewritten to dead. origin/main: projection alive 0/7, actor unchanged (no death). The engine reaches this without any model status choice: a persistent summon (start_effect kind summoning, actors:[{combatantId,campaignActorId:'wolf'}]) knocked out to 0/unconscious, then end_effect(reason:'ruled') — the actor-link cleanup (activeEffects.ts:2388-2405) sets status 'inactive' at 0 HP — and the next start_encounter with that actor projects 0/dead and kills the canonical wolf. Nothing in either result signals a death, and no tool can undo it. Same derivation also turns a 0-HP monster actor with status 'alive' (reachable via update_combatant status:'alive' on a knockout) into dead where main projected alive.
Minimal fix: in that derivation, a monster-rules actor at 0 HP whose status is not 'dead' and has no terminal cause projects as 'unconscious' (the knockout state) rather than 'dead' — at minimum for unconscious/escaped/inactive; alive/unknown at 0 should follow the same rule unless the owner records a decision otherwise — and the canonical actor keeps its life state (only participation status may change).
Permanent evidence: generalized — extend the existing batch-G S38 table (combatantRepairsBatchG.test.ts 'S38: projecting a monster-rules knockout keeps it unconscious') with actor status rows {escaped, inactive} at 0 HP under monster rules, plus one summon-end row, asserting projection status != dead and actor not dead after close/reopen. No new reproducer file.
Owner: combatant lifecycle / actor projection (batch-G S38 area). Required next state: repair before approval.

S42 | nit | packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:2385-2412 (actor-link cleanup: updateCampaignActor/updateCombatant status 'inactive', EncounterCombatantError => 'missing')
Requirement/authority: start_effect actors contract (cleanupOnEnd/cleanupOnBreak 'remove' takes the owned creature out of play; 'release' keeps it) and the cleanup report it returns to the model; review policy (truthful model-facing results).
Observation through registry: owned summon (campaignActorId 'wolf') opted into player-character rules, dropped to 0 => dying; end_effect(reason:'ruled') succeeds and reports the actor link as action 'missing', while the wolf remains an active dying participant (with S36 it now has an available turn and owes death saves). The dead-summon sibling also reports 'missing' for a creature that is present. Cause: 'inactive' is refused for a non-alive player-character-rules combatant (I4) and the refusal is swallowed as 'missing'. Introduced by this PR (main had no PC-rules combatants); niche reach (opting a summon into PC death rules); no corruption.
Minimal fix: report a truthful outcome (e.g. a 'retained' action with the reason) instead of 'missing', or record an explicit decision on how an owned PC-rules creature at 0 HP leaves play. Permanent evidence: one cleanup-result assertion if behaviour changes; none otherwise. Owner: .19.5.7.5 x F3 effect cleanup.
